items.label: Setup S-1
items.nl: Observed-law probability space: the record space \(\Omega=[0,1]\times\{0,1\}\times\{0,1\}\) with coordinates \(O=(X,A,Y)\), a Borel probability law \(P\) on \(\Omega\) whose covariate marginal has full support and whose conditional four-cell probabilities \(p_{ay}(P,x)\) are continuous and strictly interior, the public uniform design \(\lambda=\operatorname{Unif}[0,1]\), and the derived continuous functionals \(e,\mu_a,g,\nu,m,\theta,C,S\) with the H\"older seminorm \([f]_\gamma\), the logistic map \(\ell\) and its inverse \(\operatorname{logit}\). The models \(\mathcal L\), \(\mathcal M(\alpha,\beta)\), \(\mathcal M_r(\alpha,\beta)\) are sets of such laws indexed by public exponents \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal D\) and a radius \(r\in[0,1/2]\).

items.label: Setup S-4
items.nl: Converse and causal layer: the full-data law \(\widetilde P_{P,\Gamma}\) on \((X,Y^0,Y^1,A)\) built from a measurable coupling kernel \(\Gamma\) with margins \(\mu_0,\mu_1\); scalar calibration maps \(\mathfrak c,\mathfrak B,\mathfrak q,\mathsf G,\mathsf T,\mathfrak H,\mathfrak p\) of margins \(\xi,\upsilon\) and signed amplitudes \(\eta,\zeta,\delta\) with within-cell coordinate \(u\); and finite sign-indexed priors: \(\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^{k+1}\) uniform, the shared-endpoint sign field \(\mathsf Z_{k,\sigma}\), and the \(n\)-record mixtures they induce.

items.label: Definition P-3
items.nl: For every \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal D\) and \(r\in[0,1/2]\), \(\mathcal M_r(\alpha,\beta)=\{P\in\mathcal M(\alpha,\beta):|\theta(P)|\le r\}\).

items.label: Definition P-4
items.nl: For every \(n\ge1\) and \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal D\), \[\mathcal A_n(\alpha,\beta)=\{I:\Omega^n\times[0,1]\to\mathcal C\text{ Borel, with measurable coverage events and length}:\inf_{P\in\mathcal M(\alpha,\beta)}(P^{\otimes n}\otimes\lambda)\{\theta(P)\in I(\mathcal O,U)\}\ge0.90\}.\]

items.label: Definition P-6
items.nl: Sample \(X\sim\lambda\), then \((Y^0,Y^1)\mid X=x\sim\Gamma(P,x)\), then \(A\mid(X,Y^0,Y^1)\sim\operatorname{Bernoulli}\{e(P,X)\}\), and set \(Y=(1-A)Y^0+AY^1\). This defines \(\widetilde P_{P,\Gamma}\).

items.label: Definition P-8
items.nl:
For \(n\ge2\), put
\[
q_{\mathrm{rank}}(n)=7+3\lceil\log_2 n\rceil,\qquad
R_C=n^{2/(2\alpha+2\beta+1)},\qquad R_S=n^{2/(4\beta+1)}.
\]
For a positive integer \(b\), compute \(\lceil\log_2b\rceil\) by integer comparisons as the least nonnegative integer \(q\) with \(2^q\ge b\). Fix an admissible engine \(\mathsf E\) and a naming policy \(\mathsf N\). Query the exponent names at this one public precision and intersect with \([0,1]\), \([0,1/4]\). First compute the exponent ranges in the two displayed powers by exact rational range operations, then apply the positive-integer-base power map of this same engine at precision \(q_{\mathrm{rank}}(n)\). If the resulting boxes are \([a_C,b_C]\), \([a_S,b_S]\), define
\[
k_C(n,\alpha,\beta;\mathsf E,\mathsf N)=\lceil b_C\rceil,\qquad
k_S(n,\alpha,\beta;\mathsf E,\mathsf N)=\lceil b_S\rceil.
\]
The ranks are fixed before sampling because the engine is fixed and public exponent names depend only on the public exponents. Alternate engines or names may yield different integers. Width, factor bounds, and finite termination are conclusions of the realization lemma, not additional selection rules or assumptions.

items.label: Definition P-9
items.nl:
For \(n\ge2\), let \(k_C=k_C(n,\alpha,\beta;\mathsf E,\mathsf N)\) and \(k_S=k_S(n,\alpha,\beta;\mathsf E,\mathsf N)\) be the ranks selected using the same admissible engine \(\mathsf E\) and public exponent names selected by \(\mathsf N\) in the fixed-budget resolution construction. With these same selected integers define the exact real sample coordinates
\[
\widehat C_n=\frac1n\sum_{i=1}^n A_iY_i-\mathbb U_{n,k_C}(A,Y),\qquad
\widehat S_n=\mathbb U_{n,k_S}\big(A(1-Y),(1-A)Y\big).
\]
The upper algorithm uses that same engine to enclose these finite sums from the supplied covariate names; it never substitutes a separately chosen rank. The coordinates are statistics, distinct from their targets \(C(P),S(P)\).

items.label: Definition P-11
items.nl:
The represented algorithm returns \([-1/2,1/2]\) at \(n=1\). For \(n\ge2\) it first selects \(k_C,k_S\) using the fixed admissible engine \(\mathsf E\), the public names selected by \(\mathsf N\), and the fixed rank budget, and uses exactly these integers in the coordinate estimates. Put \(s=\alpha+\beta\) and
\[
V_n(k)=10/n+4k/\{n(n-1)\},\quad
b_C=8k_C^{-s}+\sqrt{20V_n(k_C)},\quad
b_S=25k_S^{-2\beta}+\sqrt{20V_n(k_S)}.
\]
For \(\operatorname{clip}_{[l,u]}(v)=\max\{l,\min(u,v)\}\), define
\[
c_\pm=\widehat C_n\pm b_C,\quad
s_\pm=\operatorname{clip}_{[s_0,1]}(\widehat S_n\pm b_S),\quad
F(c,d)=\log\!\left(\operatorname{clip}_{[\exp(-1/2),\exp(1/2)]}(1+c/d)\right),
\]
where \(s_0=1/512\) is the fixed denominator lower bound from \cref{obj:lem:observable-odds}.
\[
L=\min\{F(c_-,s_-),F(c_-,s_+)\},\qquad
R=\max\{F(c_+,s_-),F(c_+,s_+)\}.
\]
These are ideal exact-real expressions used to certify the represented output, not a separate algorithm requiring canonical names. Let
\[
K=\max\{k_C,k_S\},\qquad
q_{\mathrm{end}}(n,k_C,k_S)=44+\lceil\log_2(n+1)\rceil+4\lceil\log_2(K+1)\rceil.
\]
At this one precision query the supplied names of both exponents and all observed covariates, and evaluate the displayed finite expressions using the same engine \(\mathsf E\) at precision \(q_{\mathrm{end}}\), its primitive maps, and exact rational range operations in the displayed expression tree. The integer ranks are retained from the rank step. If the resulting endpoint enclosures are \([L_-,L_+]\) and \([R_-,R_+]\), return the closed rational interval
\[
[\max\{-1/2,L_-\},\ \min\{1/2,R_+\}].
\]
For \(0<\beta<1/4\), \(\beta<\alpha\le1\), and \(n\ge2\), the realization lemma proves that every valid input yields endpoint widths at most \(1/n\), a nonempty outward rational interval with at most \(2/n\) additional length, and termination after the two fixed budgets. These are consequences of the primitive contracts; no precision search or fallback is used on valid inputs. For an admissible engine \(\mathsf E\) and Borel naming policy \(\mathsf N\), write the resulting sample map as \(I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)\). It receives no \(r\) and no unknown nuisance. Different admissible engines or valid names can yield different rational endpoints.

items.label: Definition P-12
items.nl:
For every admissible engine \(\mathsf E\) and admissible naming policy \(\mathsf N\), define
\[
\rho_n(\alpha,\beta;r)=d_n(\alpha,\beta;r),\qquad
\big(\rho,I^{\mathrm{up}}_{\mathsf E,\mathsf N}\big)\quad\text{is the frontier pair},\qquad
I^\star_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}=I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}.
\]
The single concrete sequence is exactly
\[
I_n^\star=I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E_0,\mathsf N_0},
\]
where \(\mathsf E_0\) is constructed by the concrete-engine lemma and \(\mathsf N_0\) is the dyadic-floor policy. Every interval is the literal output of the same fixed-budget expression tree evaluated by its supplied fixed engine on its supplied valid names. Different engines or names may return different certified rational intervals; no equality across engines or names is asserted. The observed-law coordinates \((C,S)\), separate projection resolutions, and joint inversion remain unchanged. The represented inputs are \((n,\alpha,\beta,\mathcal O)\), their names chosen by \(\mathsf N\), and the independently fixed engine \(\mathsf E\). The evaluation radius \(r\) is not an interval input.

The converse uses the unchanged continuous calibrated priors: legal native propensity and prognosis perturbations, one common scalar effect per draw, analytic singleton matching, and factorization only across disjoint latent-sign components conditional on the original covariates. It is independent of both engine and naming policy.

items.label: Definition P-13
items.nl:
The arguments \(\xi,\upsilon\) are scalar margins near \(1/2\). Put
\[
d=\exp(t)-1,\quad v_*=\xi(1-\xi)\upsilon(1-\upsilon),\quad
L_*=1+d\{\xi(1-\upsilon)+(1-\xi)\upsilon\},\quad
D(t)=\int_0^1\exp(st)\,ds,
\]
where \(s\) is an integration variable. On the domain where the displayed square root and denominator are positive, define
\[
\mathfrak c(t,\xi,\upsilon)
=\frac{2dv_*}{L_*+\sqrt{L_*^2-4d^2v_*}},\qquad
\mathfrak B(t,\xi,\upsilon)
=\frac{2D(t)v_*}{L_*+\sqrt{L_*^2-4d^2v_*}}.
\]
For two auxiliary independent uniform signs \(\epsilon_0,\epsilon_1\), write
\[
Z_u=\epsilon_0\cos(\pi u/2)+\epsilon_1\sin(\pi u/2).
\]
Use the fixed branch domains supplied by Lemma~\(\mathrm{exact\mbox{-}calibrations}\) and its existing proof. Write \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mix}}>0\) for the radius of its signed open amplitude square. On
\[
|\eta|<\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mix}},\qquad
|\zeta|<\varepsilon_{\mathrm{mix}},\qquad u\in[0,1],
\]
define \(\mathfrak q(\eta,\zeta,u)\) to be the unique real root \(q\in(3/4,5/4)\) of
\[
16E\mathfrak B(32\eta\zeta,1/2-\eta qZ_u,1/2+\zeta Z_u)-q=0.
\]
Thus, on this proved domain, \(\mathfrak q\) is identified with the Lean bracket selector \texttt{mixedRoot}, whose selection bracket is exactly \((3/4,5/4)\). The smaller closed amplitude squares used in the support and mixture results lie inside this same proved domain. Set \(p_*=2/5\), \(v_*=p_*(1-p_*)=6/25\) when defining the following separate fair-prior maps:
\[
\mathsf G(t,\xi)=\frac{\exp(t)\xi}{1+\{\exp(t)-1\}\xi},\qquad B_*=1+\{\exp(t)-1\}p_*,
\]
\[
\mathsf T(t,\delta)=t+
\log\left(1-\frac{\{\exp(t)-1\}\delta^2}{p_*B_*}\right)
-\log\left(1+\frac{\{\exp(t)-1\}\delta^2}{(1-p_*)B_*}\right).
\]
On the certified fair core \(0\le t\le1/4\), whenever \(t\delta\ne0\), define the normalized fair-matching residual by
\[
\mathfrak H(t,\delta,\xi,u)
=\frac{E\mathsf G(t,\xi+\delta Z_u)-\mathsf G(\mathsf T(t,\delta),\xi)}{t\delta^2}.
\]
Let \(\mathfrak H\) also denote the removable smooth extension of this residual to the fixed open neighborhood supplied by the calibration certificate. The quotient identity is asserted on the certified core; the surrounding neighborhood supplies smoothness across \(t=0\), \(\delta=0\), and the spatial endpoints.
For the fair branch, write \(\varepsilon_{\mathrm{fair}}>0\) for the signed amplitude radius and \(b\in(0,1/10)\) for the fixed sufficiently small bracket half-width about \(p_*\) chosen in that same proof. Its fair parameter domain contains
\[
0\le t\le1/4,\qquad |\delta|<\varepsilon_{\mathrm{fair}},
\qquad u\in[0,1],
\]
and the fixed open neighborhood of these parameters used there, including signed parameters across \(t=0\) and the spatial endpoints. On this proved neighborhood the denominators and logarithm arguments in the fair formulas are positive. At \(t=0\) or \(\delta=0\), \(\mathfrak H\) means the removable smooth extension established on this neighborhood by that lemma. Define \(\mathfrak p(t,\delta,u)\) there to be the unique real root \(\xi\) in the one fixed bracket
\[
p_*-b<\xi<p_*+b
\]
of \(\mathfrak H(t,\delta,\xi,u)=0\). On this proved domain it is identified with the Lean bracket selector \texttt{fairRoot}: that selector uses \((3/10,1/2)\), and its selected root is the same root in \((p_*-b,p_*+b)\) on the certified neighborhood. The smaller closed amplitude neighborhood used in the support and mixture results is contained in this fair domain, uniformly over \(t\in[0,1/4]\) and \(u\in[0,1]\).

These definitions name the branches on their proved domains; existence, uniqueness, regularity, and matching are established by Lemma~\(\mathrm{exact\mbox{-}calibrations}\) and its existing proof. Values of the local calibration branches outside these proved branch domains are immaterial to every delivered result and are left unspecified. The identification with the Lean selectors is restricted to the proved domains.

items.label: Definition P-14
items.nl:
For an integer \(k\ge1\), put \(\Delta=1/k\) and let \(\sigma=(\sigma_0,\ldots,\sigma_k)\) have independent uniform sign coordinates. On the cell \(j\Delta\le x\le(j+1)\Delta\), where \(0\le j<k\), put
\[
u=(x-j\Delta)/\Delta,\qquad
\mathsf Z_{k,\sigma}(x)=\sigma_j\cos(\pi u/2)+\sigma_{j+1}\sin(\pi u/2).
\]
Use either cell at a shared endpoint. For signed amplitudes \(\eta,\zeta\), set
\[
e_0(x)=1/2+\eta\mathfrak q(\eta,\zeta,u)\mathsf Z_{k,\sigma}(x),\quad
e_1(x)=1/2-\eta\mathfrak q(\eta,\zeta,u)\mathsf Z_{k,\sigma}(x),\quad
m_\sigma(x)=1/2+\zeta\mathsf Z_{k,\sigma}(x).
\]
For \(b\in\{0,1\}\) set \(c_0(x)=0\) and
\(c_1(x)=\mathfrak c(32\eta\zeta,e_1(x),m_\sigma(x))\). Define the four conditional cells of \(P_{b,\sigma}\) by
\[
\begin{aligned}
p_{11}&=e_bm_\sigma+c_b,&p_{10}&=e_b(1-m_\sigma)-c_b,\\
p_{01}&=(1-e_b)m_\sigma-c_b,&p_{00}&=(1-e_b)(1-m_\sigma)+c_b.
\end{aligned}
\]
Their covariate law is \(\lambda\).
For \(0\le t\le1/4\), define the separate fair families \(P_{t,\sigma}\) and \(P_{*,t,\delta}\) with covariate law \(\lambda\) and treatment probability \(1/2\) by the respective control and treated risks
\[
\begin{array}{c|cc}
&\mu_0(x)&\mu_1(x)\\ \hline
P_{t,\sigma}&
\mathfrak p(t,\delta,u)+\delta\mathsf Z_{k,\sigma}(x)&
\mathsf G\{t,\mathfrak p(t,\delta,u)+\delta\mathsf Z_{k,\sigma}(x)\}\\
P_{*,t,\delta}&\mathfrak p(t,\delta,u)&
\mathsf G\{\mathsf T(t,\delta),\mathfrak p(t,\delta,u)\}.
\end{array}
\]
These formulas name probability laws only on the positive-cell calibration neighborhood. Let
\[
Q_b=2^{-(k+1)}\sum_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^{k+1}}P_{b,\sigma}^{\otimes n},
\qquad
Q_t=2^{-(k+1)}\sum_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^{k+1}}P_{t,\sigma}^{\otimes n}.
\]
Thus the signs are drawn once for a whole sample; the mixtures contain exactly \(n\) original records.

items.label: Definition P-15
items.nl:
A dyadic name for a real number \(v\) is a sequence of closed intervals with dyadic rational endpoints, nested by inclusion, containing \(v\), and having width at most \(2^{-q}\) at integer precision \(q\ge0\). Their product coding uses the discrete measurable structure on rational responses. An admissible naming policy is a sequence of choices, one for each \(n\). At each sample size the policy \(\mathsf N\) consists of Borel choices of valid names for \(\alpha,\beta\) as functions of the public pair \((\alpha,\beta)\) alone, and Borel choices of valid names for the \(n\) observed covariates as functions of \((\alpha,\beta,\mathcal O)\). In particular, a public exponent name is fixed before the sample is drawn. Name selection is an input convention rather than a property imposed on \(P\). The interval receives the selected names and the exact binary labels. The policy \(\mathsf N_0\) chooses, for every real input \(v\),
\[
[2^{-q}\lfloor2^qv\rfloor,\;2^{-q}(\lfloor2^qv\rfloor+1)]\qquad(q\ge0).
\]
This convention is valid even at dyadic inputs. It is used only to select one concrete member of the policy-indexed interval family.

Names and arithmetic engines are separate inputs. The naming policy does not select or modify the arithmetic engine. Compact-domain intersections are performed at the rank step only: the queried public exponent-name boxes are intersected with the known compact boxes \(\alpha\in[0,1]\) and \(\beta\in[0,1/4]\), exactly as specified in the resolution construction. At that rank step, a syntactically malformed queried prefix or an empty intersection may return the full effect interval. At the endpoint precision, the supplied exponent and observed-covariate name boxes are queried raw and passed to the endpoint expression tree without compact-domain intersections, exactly as specified in the upper construction. The integer ranks selected at the rank step are retained. The dyadic-floor policy \(\mathsf N_0\) is a convention for selecting one concrete member; outputs may vary across valid names, and no output invariance across names is asserted.

items.label: Definition P-16
items.nl:
An arithmetic engine \(\mathsf E\) is a deterministic collection of maps on closed rational intervals. Its precision input is an integer \(q\ge0\); write \(\epsilon_q=2^{-q}\). It includes a rational enclosure of \(\pi\), interval exponential and cosine on every bounded rational interval, interval logarithm on \([a,b]\) with rational \(0<a\le b\), interval square root on \([a,b]\) with rational \(0\le a\le b\), and interval power \(b^v\) for a positive integer \(b\) and a rational exponent interval contained in \([-3,3]\). Here \(a,b,v,q\) are bound primitive arguments, and the integer base is a separate argument from an interval endpoint. The engine also includes the exact rational range operations for addition, subtraction, multiplication, division when the denominator interval avoids zero, minimum, maximum, intersection, and clipping. For example, the range of the minimum of two boxes \([a,b],[c,d]\) is \([\min(a,c),\min(b,d)]\); products use the four corner extrema. Division uses the reciprocal range followed by multiplication. Clipping is evaluated by these exact minimum and maximum operations.

Admissibility consists of the following primitive contracts. Each returned interval contains the real image of its input box. For the monotone primitives exponential, logarithm, square root, and positive-integer-base power, the returned endpoints differ outward from the corresponding exact range endpoints by at most \(\epsilon_q\) each. The enclosure of \(\pi\) has the same endpoint-excess bound and is contained in \([3,4]\). For cosine, the engine encloses its value at the rational midpoint with outward endpoint excess at most \(\epsilon_q\), enlarges by half the input argument width on each side, and intersects with \([-1,1]\). Its returned width is therefore at most the input width plus \(2\epsilon_q\). Exponential and power outputs have positive lower endpoints; square-root outputs have nonnegative lower endpoints. A logarithm is evaluated only on a box with positive rational lower endpoint, and division only on a box avoiding zero. These are primitive-domain contracts, not rank or final-endpoint conclusions.

Every map is defined by a finite rational recurrence, with its iteration count bounded by a specified public integer function of the rational range bounds, the integer base if present, and \(q\). Rational comparisons and integer arithmetic are allowed; access to a real input other than its supplied rational box is forbidden. An engine is fixed independently of all public exponents, sample sizes, records, laws, naming policies, evaluation radii, and unknown nuisances. Distinct admissible engines may return distinct rational enclosures. No final precision budget or statistical property is part of engine admissibility.

items.label: Lemma L-1
items.nl: For every \(P\in\mathcal M(\alpha,\beta)\), \[C(P)=\{\exp(\theta(P))-1\}S(P),\quad S(P)\ge s_0,\quad \theta(P)=\log\{1+C(P)/S(P)\}.\] For every allowed \(\Gamma\), the extension \(\widetilde P_{P,\Gamma}\) has observed marginal \(P\), satisfies consistency and conditional treatment exchangeability, and for every \(x\in[0,1]\), \[\operatorname{logit}E_{\widetilde P_{P,\Gamma}}(Y^1\mid X=x)-\operatorname{logit}E_{\widetilde P_{P,\Gamma}}(Y^0\mid X=x)=\theta(P).\]

items.label: Lemma L-2
items.nl: Under \(P\circ X^{-1}=\lambda\), for every \(0<\gamma\le1\), every continuous \(f\), and every \(k\ge1\), \[\|f-\Pi_kf\|_{L^2(\lambda)}\le5[f]_\gamma k^{-\gamma}.\] For every pair of bounded marks \(W,V\), every \(k\ge1\), and every \(n\ge2\), \[E_P\mathbb U_{n,k}(W,V)=\langle\Pi_kw,\Pi_kv\rangle_{L^2(\lambda)},\quad \langle w,v\rangle_{L^2(\lambda)}-E_P\mathbb U_{n,k}(W,V)=\langle w-\Pi_kw,v-\Pi_kv\rangle_{L^2(\lambda)},\] \[\operatorname{Var}_P\{\mathbb U_{n,k}(W,V)\}\le4/n+2k/\{n(n-1)\}.\]

items.label: Lemma L-3
items.nl: For every \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal D\), every \(n\ge1\), and every \(0\le r\le1/2\), \[J_n(\alpha,\beta;r)\ge\frac3{16}n^{-1/2}.\] The comparison may use the constant-nuisance Bernoulli subexperiment \(g(P,x)=\nu(P,x)=0\), with scalar effects zero and \(1/(4\sqrt n)\).

items.label: Lemma L-4
items.nl:
Let \(F\) be a continuously differentiable real function on an open subset of \(\mathbb R^{d+1}\), with arguments \((\mathbf b,\chi)\in\mathbb R^d\times\mathbb R\).
If \(F(\mathbf b_0,\chi_0)=0\) and \(\partial_\chi F(\mathbf b_0,\chi_0)\ne0\), then, locally, its zero set is the graph of a unique continuously differentiable function \(\chi=q(\mathbf b)\).

items.label: Lemma L-5
items.nl:
There is an absolute positive amplitude neighborhood on which the maps in the calibration definition are well defined and have the following properties.
The branch \(\mathfrak c(t,\xi,\upsilon)\) gives a positive four-cell table with margins \(\xi,\upsilon\) and odds ratio \(\exp(t)\), and \(\mathfrak B=\mathfrak c/t\) off zero, with
\(\mathfrak B(0,\xi,\upsilon)=\xi(1-\xi)\upsilon(1-\upsilon)\).
The root \(\mathfrak q(\eta,\zeta,u)\), for both signed amplitudes and \(u\in[0,1]\), is smooth, lies in \((3/4,5/4)\), and satisfies
\[
\mathfrak q(\eta,\zeta,0)=\mathfrak q(\eta,\zeta,1),\qquad
E\mathfrak c(32\eta\zeta,1/2-\eta\mathfrak q Z_u,1/2+\zeta Z_u)
=2\eta\zeta\mathfrak q .
\]
It is even in each amplitude, and
\[
\mathfrak q(0,\zeta,u)=1-4\zeta^2,\qquad
\mathfrak q(\eta,0,u)+4\eta^2\mathfrak q(\eta,0,u)^2=1.
\]
For \(0\le t\le1/4\), the fair root \(\mathfrak p(t,\delta,u)\) is smooth through \(t=0\) and \(\delta=0\), is even in \(\delta\), and satisfies
\[
\begin{split}
&\mathfrak p(t,\delta,0)=\mathfrak p(t,\delta,1)=2/5,\quad
\mathfrak p(t,0,u)=\mathfrak p(0,\delta,u)=2/5,\\
&E\mathsf G\{t,\mathfrak p(t,\delta,u)+\delta Z_u\}
=\mathsf G\{\mathsf T(t,\delta),\mathfrak p(t,\delta,u)\}.
\end{split}
\]
On a smaller closed neighborhood all fixed-order derivatives of both roots and of the actual four-cell formulas are uniformly bounded. For an absolute finite \(M\),
\[
|\mathfrak p(t,\delta,u)-2/5|+|\partial_u\mathfrak p(t,\delta,u)|\le M\delta^2.
\]
After reducing the amplitude neighborhood if needed,
\[
3t\delta^2\le t-\mathsf T(t,\delta)\le6t\delta^2,\qquad
t/2\le\mathsf T(t,\delta)\le t.
\]

items.label: Lemma L-6
items.nl:
There are absolute constants \(0<\varepsilon\le1/100\) and \(M\ge1\), chosen jointly, such that the following holds for every \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal D\), every integer \(k\ge1\), and every sign vector \(\sigma\).
With \(\eta=\varepsilon k^{-\alpha}\), \(\zeta=\varepsilon k^{-\beta}\), the mixed laws belong to \(\mathcal M(\alpha,\beta)\), have effects
\[
\theta(P_{0,\sigma})=0,\qquad
\theta(P_{1,\sigma})=32\eta\zeta,
\]
and their sign-averaged four-cell singleton tables agree at every \(x\).
With \(\delta=\varepsilon k^{-\beta}\) and any \(0\le t\le1/4\), both fair laws belong to \(\mathcal M(\alpha,\beta)\), have effects \(t\) and \(\mathsf T(t,\delta)\), respectively, and the random law's averaged singleton table equals the deterministic comparator's table at every \(x\).
All these supports have continuous native propensity and prognosis logits satisfying exactly the envelopes and seminorm bounds in the prescribed model, including \(\alpha=1\).
The same jointly chosen constants certify the signed closed amplitude box
\[
|\eta|\le\varepsilon,\qquad |\zeta|\le\varepsilon,\qquad |\delta|\le\varepsilon.
\]
The actual one-record densities are smooth in their amplitude arguments on an open neighborhood of this closed box, including through zero amplitudes. Throughout this whole same closed box, for every integer \(k\ge1\), every sign vector \(\sigma\), every covariate \(x\), and every fair center \(t\in[0,1/4]\), every one-record density relative to uniform four-label measure lies in \([1/2,2]\), and the absolute values of all its first and second amplitude partial derivatives are at most this same \(M\). These derivatives include the mixed \(\eta,\zeta\) derivative and the deterministic fair comparator's \(\delta\)-derivatives. Throughout this whole same closed box, the mixed laws' sign-averaged four-cell singleton tables agree at every \(x\), and, for every \(t\in[0,1/4]\), the fair random law's sign-averaged singleton table equals the deterministic comparator's table at every \(x\).

items.label: Lemma L-7
items.nl:
Fix one joint absolute certificate \(0<\varepsilon\le1/100\), \(M\ge1\) supplied by Lemma~\(\mathrm{calibrated\mbox{-}support}\). Use the finite mixtures \(Q_0,Q_1,Q_t\) and comparator of the continuous calibrated-prior definition with signed amplitudes in that certificate's same closed box
\[
|\eta|\le\varepsilon,\qquad |\zeta|\le\varepsilon,\qquad |\delta|\le\varepsilon.
\]
Define
\[
\mathcal H^2(Q,Q')=\int(\sqrt{dQ/dR}-\sqrt{dQ'/dR})^2\,dR,
\]
where \(R\) is any common dominating measure. There are absolute finite \(C_{\mathrm{mix}}>0\) and \(\kappa>0\) such that for all positive integers \(n,k\) with \(n/k\le\kappa\),
\[
\mathcal H^2(Q_0,Q_1)\le C_{\mathrm{mix}}\frac{n^2}{k}\eta^2\zeta^2,\qquad
\mathcal H^2(Q_t,P_{*,t,\delta}^{\otimes n})\le C_{\mathrm{mix}}\frac{n^2}{k}\delta^4.
\]
The bounds hold uniformly over \(t\in[0,1/4]\) and contain no singleton remainder. One may take
\(\kappa=1/\{96\exp(1)\}\) and
\(C_{\mathrm{mix}}=96\exp(2)\,8^2M^4\), using exactly the same \(M\) from the fixed joint certificate of Lemma~\(\mathrm{calibrated\mbox{-}support}\).

items.label: Lemma L-8
items.nl:
For every admissible arithmetic engine \(\mathsf E\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:arithmetic-engine} and admissible Borel naming policy \(\mathsf N\) in the sense of \cref{obj:def:dyadic-name-convention}, the unchanged public budgets
\[
q_{\mathrm{rank}}(n)=7+3\lceil\log_2n\rceil,\qquad
q_{\mathrm{end}}(n,k_C,k_S)=44+\lceil\log_2(n+1)\rceil+4\lceil\log_2(K+1)\rceil,
\quad K=\max\{k_C,k_S\},
\]
are sufficient for every \(n\ge2\). Each rank-target enclosure has width at most one; for its true target \(R\), its selected rank obeys \(R\le k<R+2\le3R\). Each ideal final endpoint enclosure has width at most \(1/n\). The literal output \(I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}\) contains the ideal closed interval, has additional length at most \(2/n\), and is a nonempty rational closed connected interval in \([-1/2,1/2]\). Both computations terminate on every valid input after their two prescribed finite input-prefix budgets and finite engine recurrences. The output map is Borel. These conclusions follow only from the primitive contracts, uniformly over engines and valid names; equality of outputs across engines or names is not asserted. Independently, the dyadic-floor policy \(\mathsf N_0\) is admissible.

items.label: Lemma L-9
items.nl: There is an explicit admissible rational arithmetic engine \(\mathsf E_0\). It is the collection of exact rational range operations and the scalar routines specified in the proof: exponential and cosine polynomials with \(m=\max\{2B^2,p+3\}\); the logarithm sum with \(N=B\{p+\lceil\log_2(8B)\rceil+2\}\); a dyadic square-root bracket from an integer square root; the Machin enclosure with \(N=p+4\) terms; and the integer-base power routine with internal precision \(q+12+3\lceil\log_2 B\rceil\). Here \(q\ge0\) is the requested precision, \(p=q+3\) except where the power routine supplies its internal precision, and \(B\) is the explicitly defined integer rational-range bound. All truncation counts, rational remainder brackets, and integer recurrences below are part of the definition of this witness. They uniquely specify finite rational expressions and satisfy all primitive contracts of the arithmetic-engine definition, independently of the statistical model, input names, ranks, and endpoint budgets.

items.label: Theorem T-1
items.nl:
The fixed-budget deterministic represented algorithm of the upper construction induces, for every admissible arithmetic engine \(\mathsf E\) and admissible Borel naming policy \(\mathsf N\) satisfying the quantitative contracts of \cref{obj:def:arithmetic-engine,obj:def:dyadic-name-convention}, a measurable interval procedure \(I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)\). For every such engine and policy, every \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal D\), and every \(n\ge1\),
\[
I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal A_n(\alpha,\beta).
\]
There is a positive finite absolute constant \(K_0\), independent of both engine and naming policy, such that for every \(n\ge1\), every \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal D\), and all \(0\le r\le1/2\),
\[
\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_r(\alpha,\beta)}E_{P^{\otimes n}}|I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)|
\le K_0 d_n(\alpha,\beta;r).
\]
In particular the bound is uniform on every nonempty compact \(\mathcal K\subset\mathcal D\). The algorithm uses the two prescribed fixed finite input precision budgets, uses finite certified rational arithmetic, and on every valid set of names returns a nonempty closed interval in \([-1/2,1/2]\) with rational endpoints. It receives neither \(r\) nor any unknown nuisance. Alternate admissible engines or valid names can give different selected ranks and output endpoints; every induced procedure has the same honesty and absolute length guarantee. Public exponent names are fixed independently of the sample as specified in the admissible naming-policy definition. At \(n=1\) the output is the full effect interval.

items.label: Theorem T-2
items.nl:
The diagnostic profile is sharp on the entire prescribed model. Throughout, admissible arithmetic engines and Borel naming policies satisfy the quantitative contracts of \cref{obj:def:arithmetic-engine,obj:def:dyadic-name-convention}. Explicitly, put
\[
\mathsf a(\alpha,\beta)=\min\left\{\frac12,\frac{2(\alpha+\beta)}{2\alpha+2\beta+1}\right\},\qquad
\mathsf b(\beta)=\frac{4\beta}{4\beta+1},\qquad
\rho_n(\alpha,\beta;r)=n^{-\mathsf a(\alpha,\beta)}+r n^{-\mathsf b(\beta)}.
\]
For every admissible arithmetic engine \(\mathsf E\) and admissible Borel naming policy \(\mathsf N\), let \(I^\star_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}=I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}\) be the output of the same fixed-budget represented algorithm in the upper construction, applied to the fixed admissible engine and valid names supplied by that policy. There are positive absolute finite constants \(c,C\), independent of both \(\mathsf E\) and \(\mathsf N\), such that for every \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal D\), every \(n\ge1\), and all \(0\le r\le1/2\),
\[
c\rho_n(\alpha,\beta;r)\le J_n(\alpha,\beta;r)
\le\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_r(\alpha,\beta)}E_{P^{\otimes n}}|I^\star_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)|
\le C\rho_n(\alpha,\beta;r).
\]
Fixing the explicit admissible engine \(\mathsf E_0\) and admissible policy \(\mathsf N_0\) gives one concrete interval \(I_n^\star=I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E_0,\mathsf N_0}\). One can take \(c_\star=c\), \(C_\star=C\), and \(n_0=1\). For every admissible engine and policy, the actual name-dependent output in the display is a deterministic, radius-independent Borel interval, globally \(90\%\)-honest for every finite sample size. It returns a nonempty closed connected interval in \([-1/2,1/2]\) with rational endpoints after its two prescribed finite precision budgets and finite rational arithmetic, and uses only its fixed admissible engine, the public exponents, their valid public names, and the \(n\) original records with their valid covariate names. Different admissible engines or policies may yield different ranks and endpoints. No equality across engines or names is asserted. The lower bound holds against every Borel honest procedure, including independent randomization, using finite priors whose every draw has a single homogeneous scalar effect and legal native propensity and prognosis logits in the same model.

There is no logarithmic factor. The true numerator transition is \(\alpha+\beta=1/2\), including equality. The radius transition is
\[
r\asymp n^{-(\mathsf a-\mathsf b)},\qquad
\mathsf a-\mathsf b=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\frac{2(\alpha-\beta)}{(2\alpha+2\beta+1)(4\beta+1)},&\alpha+\beta\le1/2,\\[4pt]
\displaystyle\frac{1-4\beta}{2(4\beta+1)},&\alpha+\beta\ge1/2.
\end{cases}
\]
These expressions agree on the shared boundary. Both regions \(\alpha+5\beta<1/2\) and \(\beta<1/12\), their equality boundaries, and \(\alpha=1\) are covered with no additional transition or hypothesis. The constants in particular have the required uniform bounds on every compact subset of \(\mathcal D\). The result holds at \(r=0\), for every shrinking-radius sequence, and at every fixed positive radius.

items.label: Theorem T-3
items.nl:
For every \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal D\), define
\[
\mathsf a(\alpha,\beta)=
\min\left\{\frac12,\frac{2(\alpha+\beta)}{2\alpha+2\beta+1}\right\},
\qquad \mathsf b(\beta)=\frac{4\beta}{4\beta+1},\qquad
\rho_n(\alpha,\beta;r)=
n^{-\mathsf a(\alpha,\beta)}+r n^{-\mathsf b(\beta)}.
\]
The answer to the full honest-frontier question is this profile, with no logarithmic factor: \(\rho_n=d_n\). For every admissible arithmetic engine \(\mathsf E\) and admissible Borel naming policy \(\mathsf N\) satisfying the quantitative contracts of \cref{obj:def:arithmetic-engine,obj:def:dyadic-name-convention}, take \(I^\star_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}=I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}\), literally the rational output of the fixed-budget represented algorithm. There are positive finite absolute constants \(c,C\), independent of that engine and policy, such that for every \(n\ge1\), every \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal D\), and every \(r\in[0,1/2]\),
\[
c\rho_n(\alpha,\beta;r)\le J_n(\alpha,\beta;r)
\le\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_r(\alpha,\beta)}
E_{P^{\otimes n}}|I^\star_{n,\mathsf E,\mathsf N}(\alpha,\beta)|
\le C\rho_n(\alpha,\beta;r).
\]
Each such engine-and-policy output is a globally \(90\%\)-honest Borel interval at every finite sample size, receives neither \(r\) nor unknown nuisances, and terminates on every valid named input after the rank and endpoint budgets of \cref{obj:def:resolutions,obj:def:upper-handle,obj:lem:fixed-budget-realization} with nonempty rational closed connected endpoints in \([-1/2,1/2]\). Different admissible engines or names may yield different ranks and outputs, with these same guarantees. Fixing \(\mathsf E_0,\mathsf N_0\) gives one concrete sequence \(I_n^\star=I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E_0,\mathsf N_0}\). One may take \(c_\star=c\), \(C_\star=C\), and \(n_0=1\), so the constants and threshold satisfy the requested uniform bounds on every nonempty compact \(\mathcal K\subset\mathcal D\).

The converse applies to all Borel globally honest intervals, including independent algorithmic randomization, through finite priors on the same model and exactly \(n\) original records. Every prior draw has one homogeneous scalar causal coefficient and satisfies the prescribed continuous native-logit envelopes and seminorms. The sole numerator transition is \(\alpha+\beta=1/2\), including equality, and the radius transition is \(r\asymp n^{-(\mathsf a-\mathsf b)}\), where
\[
\mathsf a-\mathsf b=
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle\frac{2(\alpha-\beta)}
{(2\alpha+2\beta+1)(4\beta+1)},&\alpha+\beta\le1/2,\\[5pt]
\displaystyle\frac{1-4\beta}{2(4\beta+1)},&\alpha+\beta\ge1/2.
\end{cases}
\]
The expressions agree on their common boundary. The full regions \(\alpha+5\beta<1/2\) and \(\beta<1/12\), both equality lines, and \(\alpha=1\) require no additional restriction or transition. The same comparison holds at \(r=0\), along every shrinking-radius sequence, and at every fixed positive radius.

items.label: Theorem T-4
items.nl:
The full honest-frontier question has the positive answer
\[
\rho_n(\alpha,\beta;r)=d_n(\alpha,\beta;r)
=n^{-\min\{1/2,\,2(\alpha+\beta)/(2\alpha+2\beta+1)\}}
+r n^{-4\beta/(4\beta+1)}.
\]
There are positive finite absolute constants \(c,C\) such that, for every \((\alpha,\beta)\in\mathcal D\), every \(n\ge1\) and every \(r\in[0,1/2]\),
\[
c\rho_n(\alpha,\beta;r)\le J_n(\alpha,\beta;r)
\le\sup_{P\in\mathcal M_r(\alpha,\beta)}
E_{P^{\otimes n}}|I_n^\star(\alpha,\beta)|
\le C\rho_n(\alpha,\beta;r),
\qquad I_n^\star=I^{\mathrm{up}}_{n,\mathsf E_0,\mathsf N_0}.
\]
The arithmetic engines and Borel naming policies below satisfy the quantitative contracts of \cref{obj:def:arithmetic-engine,obj:def:dyadic-name-convention}. The constants can be chosen once for all public exponents, sample sizes and radii. One may take \(c_\star=c\), \(C_\star=C\), and \(n_0=1\), satisfying all required uniform bounds on compact subsets of \(\mathcal D\). This single sequence is radius independent, Borel and globally \(90\%\)-honest at every finite sample size. It terminates after the prescribed fixed budgets on every valid named input, with rational nonempty closed connected endpoints in \([-1/2,1/2]\), and receives no unknown nuisance. More generally, replacing \(\mathsf E_0,\mathsf N_0\) by any admissible engine \(\mathsf E\) and Borel naming policy \(\mathsf N\) gives the same comparisons and coverage with the same constants, even if the literal intervals differ.

The converse covers every Borel procedure in \(\mathcal A_n(\alpha,\beta)\), including independent randomization, using finite priors in exactly \(\mathcal M(\alpha,\beta)\) and likelihoods of exactly \(n\) original records. Every prior draw has one homogeneous scalar causal effect and legal continuous native propensity and prognosis logits. No logarithmic factor is necessary. The sole numerator transition is \(\alpha+\beta=1/2\), including equality. The radius transition is
\[
r\asymp
\begin{cases}
\displaystyle n^{-2(\alpha-\beta)/\{(2\alpha+2\beta+1)(4\beta+1)\}},&\alpha+\beta\le1/2,\\[5pt]
\displaystyle n^{-(1-4\beta)/\{2(4\beta+1)\}},&\alpha+\beta\ge1/2.
\end{cases}
\]
The expressions agree at the common boundary. Both regions \(\alpha+5\beta<1/2\) and \(\beta<1/12\), their equality boundaries, \(\alpha=1\), \(r=0\), every shrinking-radius sequence and fixed positive radii are included without any extra hypothesis.
